run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-16T19:06:03Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning on otel-demo/frontend traces to a bad rollout of the product-catalog Deployment at 19:04:12Z that set the container command to ["invalid-command"]. The only product-catalog replica can never start (runc: executable file not found in $PATH, StartError/exit 128, CrashLoopBackOff, 5 restarts), the previous healthy pod was deleted at 19:04:21Z, the product-catalog Service now has no ready endpoint addresses, and product-catalog span traffic went to zero from 19:10. Frontend error spans were zero through the 19:05:00 sample and appear from the 19:06:00 sample, on exactly the routes that need product-catalog: GET /api/products/{productId}, GET /api/recommendations and POST /api/checkout carry ERROR status on every span in the 10-minute increase ending 19:15:00, while GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart and GET /api/data carry none. The same product-catalog call appears as the only failing client operation in checkout (oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct) and recommendation (/oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts), and frontend-proxy records ingress/egress errors on the affected requests. Nodes are all Ready with no memory or disk pressure, and accounting, fraud-detection, payment and ad show no error-span increase, so the fault is localized to the product-catalog workload rather than the frontend, its dependency peers or the cluster.

claims.text: Frontend error spans were zero in every sample through 19:05:00Z and became non-zero at the 19:06:00Z sample (STATUS_CODE_ERROR 15m increase 0 -> 481.03), while frontend total span volume stayed roughly flat (13,336.7 per 5m at 18:55:00 vs 11,422.2 at 19:10:00), so the alert is an error-rate shift and not a traffic surge.

In the 10-minute increase ending 19:15:00Z, frontend server spans with STATUS_CODE_ERROR were GET /api/products/{productId} 2487.41, GET /api/recommendations 475.18 and POST /api/checkout 296.58, each with zero non-error (STATUS_CODE_UNSET) spans in the same evaluation, while GET /api/cart (504.41), POST /api/cart (889.75) and GET /api/data (484.93) had zero error spans.

Frontend's failing spans include outbound client operations grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, with counts identical to the corresponding server-side handler and 'executing api route (pages)' spans, plus tcp.connect error spans (0 -> 18.24 per 10m), indicating the frontend's outbound calls, not its own inbound handling, are where the failure originates.

Checkout's error spans are exactly oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (137.96 then 296.58 per 10m) and oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct (same values), and recommendation's are /oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts (228.13 then 478.43) and get_product_list (same values); recommendation's only other error series is a steady ~1.05 per 10m on /flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream.

frontend-proxy records STATUS_CODE_ERROR on its 'ingress' spans (1973.68 then 3290.57 per 10m) and 'router frontend egress' spans (1969.47 then 3285.16 per 10m) over the same period, i.e. the proxy observed errors on requests it routed to frontend.

product-catalog span volume was steady at ~3133-3281 per 5m through 19:05:00Z, then fell to 2563.33 (19:06), 1756.67 (19:07), 962.22 (19:08), 102.22 (19:09) and 0 from 19:10:00Z onward, while recommendation and frontend kept serving traffic.

Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog (generation 4, deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 2, Helm release otel-demo) has container 'product-catalog' with command ["invalid-command"], image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog, no readinessProbe and no livenessProbe, and status Available=False with reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable, unavailableReplicas 1, updatedReplicas 1.

Pod product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l (owner ReplicaSet product-catalog-fcf7564cf, created 19:04:29Z) has restartCount 5, ready=false, started=false, state waiting/CrashLoopBackOff ('back-off 2m40s restarting failed container'), and lastState terminated with reason StartError, exitCode 128 and message: failed to create containerd task ... OCI runtime create failed: runc create failed: unable to start container process: error during container init: exec: "invalid-command": executable file not found in $PATH; its imageID is sha256:5af68959300c804e71176aa8071abd30d1209771762e006c9fe7843561ab7b6a.

Pod and ReplicaSet events for product-catalog record the rollout and failure sequence: 19:04:12Z Scheduled and SuccessfulCreate of product-catalog-fcf7564cf-2fvnx; 19:04:16Z Pulled and Created container; 19:04:17Z Failed 'exec: "invalid-command": executable file not found in $PATH' plus BackOff; 19:04:21Z Killing of product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-wzpwm and SuccessfulDelete of it, with old ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc scaled 1 -> 0; 19:04:29Z new pod product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l created (ReplicaSet scaled 0 -> 1); 19:07:42Z Failed (count 6); 19:09:44Z BackOff (count 25); 19:10:24Z Created container again.

Service 'product-catalog' currently has no ready addresses at all: its only subset contains notReadyAddresses [100.96.2.148] targeting pod product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l on node i-0797cc64ce8b8a966, so there is no healthy backend for callers.

ReplicaSet product-catalog-fcf7564cf (created 19:04:12Z, owner product-catalog) is the only ReplicaSet created after 18:36:15Z in otel-demo; every other workload's ReplicaSet dates from 18:34:11-18:34:13Z, and the old product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc now has replicas 0, showing a product-catalog-only rollout.
All five nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure=False and DiskPressure=False, including node i-0797cc64ce8b8a966 where the failing product-catalog pod runs.

Error spans by service over the incident period show accounting 0, fraud-detection 0 and payment 0 across all samples, and ad only ~1.05-1.08 per 10m both at 18:55 and 19:15 (the same level as before the incident), so no error evidence exists for those services. Series for cart, currency, email, shipping, quote, image-provider, kafka and load-generator were not returned by that query, so their error counts remain unknown rather than zero.

Frontend's routes that do not need product-catalog stayed error-free at the 19:15:00Z evaluation: GET /api/cart 504.41, POST /api/cart 889.75 and GET /api/data 484.93 spans, all STATUS_CODE_UNSET with zero ERROR, so the frontend runtime itself continued serving requests while product-catalog-dependent routes failed.

Rejected: a node-level or resource-pressure fault as the cause of the frontend errors. All nodes are Ready without memory/disk pressure, the product-catalog container never reaches process start at all, and the failure text identifies a missing executable rather than a resource or scheduling problem.

Rejected: a frontend-side network or DNS problem reaching its backends. If the break were on the frontend side, product-catalog would keep receiving traffic from its other callers; instead product-catalog's own span volume fell to zero, its Service has no ready endpoint, and recommendation and checkout keep serving while only their ProductCatalogService calls error.

Rejected as the cause of this alert: the fraud-detection pod OOMKilled restart. Pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-8bpr4 shows restartCount 1 with lastState terminated reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, but the termination time is not visible in the returned object and fraud-detection has zero error spans in every sample, so nothing ties that restart to the frontend request error rate.

Mechanism: because the single product-catalog replica cannot start and the previous pod was deleted, Service product-catalog has no ready endpoint; the frontend's gRPC calls to ProductCatalogService (directly, and via recommendation's ListProducts and checkout's GetProduct) fail, and the frontend returns errors on /api/products/{productId}, /api/recommendations and /api/checkout, which is what the RequestErrorRate warning measures. No span parent references were available for the incident window, so the call edges are inferred from span and operation names and from metric correlation rather than from observed parent-child links.

Restore Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog to a startable command (remove the ["invalid-command"] override or set the image's real entrypoint for ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog), then confirm pod readiness, a non-empty ready endpoint set for Service product-catalog, and recovery of the frontend error rate.

Harden the rollout so a bad container command cannot remove the last healthy replica: the deployment currently has no readinessProbe or livenessProbe and its RollingUpdate (maxSurge 25%, maxUnavailable 25% of a 1-replica deployment) replaced the only old pod at 19:04:21Z before any new pod became ready; add a readiness probe on port 8080 and review the strategy.

gaps: Who or what changed the product-catalog container command (and any accompanying Helm value change) is unknown: the change_history integration is listed as not_integrated, so the rollout's authoring source cannot be read; the Deployment shows only Helm release annotations (meta.helm.sh/release-name=otel-demo) and revision 2.

Jaeger trace detail for the incident window is unavailable: traces_search for frontend returned no_data (3ea0d349-cbfd-43b0-956b-ff57cb26a740-t1:39ac040b-a76d-4108-a04b-d93cb13aea81) and traces_search_by_tags with error=true returned no_data (451032a7-1699-4460-84b7-f3f29939948a-t2:ccbdd72d-2eea-4e8c-ae27-ce5911cc5108); one product-catalog traces_search errored with RESULT_TOO_LARGE and was not read (8447a5f1-1539-488c-aba0-352799d46c86-t2:15827857-9b5d-4192-8fd9-68680cd6a6fb), and its retained result was never read. Per-span gRPC status codes, error messages and parent-child references for the failing calls therefore remain unknown.

Application logs are unavailable: fetch_pod_logs for product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l returned no_data with 0 lines (451032a7-1699-4460-84b7-f3f29939948a-t0:35ae26ae-d353-45e5-bd53-bf53122e36a0), consistent with a container that never starts but not proof of it, and fetch_pod_logs for frontend-675fd7b5c5-9f6l5 returned no_data both unfiltered (078ae3ac-511e-47cb-9d9e-529ff9660a75-t2:7f95c652-d56a-44f5-b6ab-f8e86362ab37) and filtered (b2ddfec7-5e33-4390-92aa-0236735bd973-t0:4e7eff16-c478-43fe-8e8c-f4124c1b0b80), so no application error text is available for either service.

The alert's own expression and the reported value 16.8667 could not be reproduced: list_prometheus_rules for rule name RequestErrorRate returned no_data (3ca6f356-4dcd-4e08-a871-ac20a76d3398-t0:49c4b304-60d5-489e-99b1-0aa068be68ff) and http_response_status_code label values for http_server_request_duration_seconds_count returned no_data (078ae3ac-511e-47cb-9d9e-529ff9660a75-t1:982b17b2-d569-4342-86dc-154a43043390), so the exact alert denominator is unknown.

gRPC client metrics are missing: rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count returned no_data for service_name=frontend (8447a5f1-1539-488c-aba0-352799d46c86-t1:fdea73c9-32b6-49c5-9068-3b0bd3d81cb9) and no rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count series matched on service_name=frontend across 19:00-19:15Z (get_label_values 8447a5f1-1539-488c-aba0-352799d46c86-t0:fd1eacf7-854e-4927-9d56-8f991eb73ae6 had no data); a get_metric_names query for rpc_client.* in 19:05-19:15 also returned no_data (c206cf9b-9656-4931-97a4-f41b02e30665-t0:2fa8af4e-3417-48c1-8f65-6c2862ad040e), and the rpc_grpc_status_code label query returned no_data (8447a5f1-1539-488c-aba0-352799d46c86-t0:fd1eacf7-854e-4927-9d56-8f991eb73ae6), so status codes such as UNAVAILABLE vs DEADLINE_EXCEEDED are unknown rather than absent.

kube-state-metrics series for the rollout were not available: kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready, kube_pod_owner and kube_replicaset_owner for otel-demo returned no_data (078ae3ac-511e-47cb-9d9e-529ff9660a75-t0:43ed23a3-4b48-4f35-9154-4911ca46f189 and b2ddfec7-5e33-4390-92aa-0236735bd973-t2:1850e0b1-3dc6-4835-a2fb-5b3b06dbd179), so the rollout's effect on those series could not be plotted; the rollout was established from Events and live object state instead.

A label-selector pod query app=product-catalog returned no_data (7adf9e24-74d8-41b5-a44c-18e3a7e48fac-t0:703fda78-940d-488a-bbce-deb3ff5431f1), so the pods' label set could not be confirmed through that selector; the product-catalog pod was instead identified by name and owner reference.

No error series were returned for cart, currency, email, shipping, quote, image-provider, kafka or load-generator, so whether those services logged any errors during the window is unknown rather than zero.
The old product-catalog pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-wzpwm was deleted at 19:04:21Z, so its image digest and previous command could not be compared with the new ReplicaSet's template.
next_steps: Identify the source of the invalid-command change to the otel-demo Helm release (chart value or GitOps commit) using the change-history system once it is integrated.

After the command is fixed, confirm the deployment reaches Available=True, the product-catalog endpoints list a ready address, and frontend STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans for /api/products/{productId}, /api/recommendations and /api/checkout return to zero.
Verify with the alerting owner which PromQL expression and denominator RequestErrorRate uses, since the rule is not present in this Prometheus target.
